The page calls these transitivity relations essentially tautological and says that they are obtained by taking inverse images of the maps cited as (194), (197), and (198). Those earlier definitions were not consulted. The formal functoriality check below is conditional and is not a verification that those particular maps satisfy the displayed identities.

Conditional mathematical check: for a functor F and composable maps f,g, if the third map is h=g∘f then F(h)=F(g)∘F(f). Thus a transitivity identity is preserved by a genuinely functorial inverse-image construction. Applying this to the particular objects in (202) still requires the cited definitions and their compatible identifications, which are outside this assigned page.

The final paragraph announces a further relation requiring the normal-crossings hypothesis. That relation is not stated on this page, so no proof or hypothesis-sufficiency claim is made. The cancelled toute la force de, the literal tt abbreviation, and the paired quote strokes remain as written.
